subject: Third-party risk: clarification on subprocessor inventory & data flow
messages:
From: Alex Morton <security@finhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: up-to-date subprocessor inventory + attestation

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking a look. As part of our procurement security assessment we need a couple of things to close the vendor review for Redwood Inference: 

1) A current subprocessor inventory (names, purpose, geographic region, whether they process PHI/PII).
2) Short attestation on whether any subprocessors hold persistent customer data at rest (and if so, encryption mechanisms + KMS provider).
3) Any recent SIG/CIS/CAIQ extracts you can share (redacted as needed).

We'd like to get this by EOD next week if possible — will add to our vendor portal once received. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if that helps.

Appreciate it,
Alex Morton
Senior Information Security Analyst
FinHealth Analytics

Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: up-to-date subprocessor inventory + attestation

Hi all — attached is the current export and a concise attestation. Summary below; full CSV attached.

Quick summary (high level):
- Total subprocessors: 14 (see attached).
- Only three subprocessors store persistent customer data: S3 (object store for customer-uploaded artifacts), Datastore-X (encrypted blob store for queued job artifacts), and LogArchiveCo (retention-only audit logs, encrypted).
- Encryption at rest: AES-256 for object stores and blobs; keys are managed by AWS KMS (customer-region key policies for Dedicated/Private customers) or HSM-backed KMS for on-prem instances where applicable.
- PHI/PII processing: marked per-row in CSV; we do not process PHI by default. Where customers opt-in to ingest PHI, subprocessors are included with enhanced contractual assurances and an enclave model for Dedicated/Private.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_inventory.csv (csv), dataflow_diagram_v2.png (png), sig-extracts-2026.pdf (pdf)

Evelyn Hart
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0172

Notes: Evelyn included a per-subprocessor column called "persistent_data_yes_no" and a KMS_field indicating KMS vendor and region. For Dedicated customers we have an option to disable third-party object store usage and instead enable in-cluster volume storage (documented in the Private deployment playbook).

From: Alex Morton <security@finhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: up-to-date subprocessor inventory + attestation

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick follow-ups: 

1) For the three subprocessors you listed as storing persistent data, can you confirm whether any of them are located in APAC/EU? We have regional-dataflow constraints.
2) The CSV column for KMS shows "aws-kms:us-west-2" for some rows; can you confirm whether customer-managed KMS keys are supported for hosted customers or only Dedicated/Private?

If it's easier, we can schedule a 20-minute walkthrough Monday morning.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.
Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morton <security@finhealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: up-to-date subprocessor inventory + attestation

Alex — quick answers inline, and attaching a short FAQ we put together for regional questions.

1) Region: Of the three that persist data, none have primary storage in APAC by default; LogArchiveCo provides EU-hosted retention buckets for customers who opt in (we show region per-row in the CSV). We will flag EU/APAC rows explicitly.

2) KMS: For hosted customers, we support Redwood-managed KMS by default (aws-kms:us-west-2). Customer-managed keys are supported for Dedicated customers and for Hosted customers who sign the customer-managed-keys addendum (see linked Drive doc). Private (on-prem) deployments always use customer-controlled KMS/HSM.

Next steps: Evelyn will update the CSV to add a "region_residency" column and a short redaction-ready SIG extract. Monica — please confirm any language you want in the customer-managed-keys addendum before we share with FinHealth.
